findings.reason: the body tells a node the current term is a full-load charge to be reduced, when the work is actually to raise a zero charge to the reference cost, and any test derived from "and not the file size" is written against behaviour that no longer exists.
findings.text: §3 asserts "A path a node must edit and a path a node is told never to open are not the same load, and today they cost the same", and at :118 that a negated clause "is currently the place it is most wrong", but `_declared_input_files` (reckon/crew/routing.py:3026) charges nothing for a mere mention and withholds a negated clause's paths, so a mention already costs zero and a write path full — the section's activation comment at :256 ("a mention costs nothing and a negated clause's paths are withheld") and its reopen comment at :277 ("the code's current answer is `zero`") both say so, contradicting the body.

findings.reason: a node cannot implement two opposite charges for one path, so the clause must be split into the different-files case (reference for the negated path, full for the write path) or a precedence rule stated.
findings.text: §3's assertion that "a path inside a negative clause is asserted to be charged as a reference even when the same path is also a declared write path elsewhere in the brief, since the two clauses are about different files in the general case and the write path must still be charged at full" states a path is charged as a reference and at full in one breath, and justifies the same-path case with a "different files in the general case" reason that does not cover it; the code's `counted` dedup (routing.py:3129) describes write paths before named files, so a path in both sets is already counted once at full — the measure gives a node no unambiguous assertion to write and no rule for the collision.

findings.reason: the node dispatched to §4 would find its central assertion impossible to satisfy and either pick a reference cost the lead has not chosen or return blocked, and the plan should state that §4 requires a nonzero reference cost (or restate the opt-out's measure) before dispatch.
findings.text: §4's measure "asserted by the same brief estimating lower with the opt-out than without it" cannot hold if §3's `reference-cost` decision (docs/plans/a-brief-should-not-cost-what-it-names.html:225, `data-choice=""`) settles at `zero`: an opted-out anchor and a plain mention would both cost zero, so "lower with the opt-out" is unsatisfiable, yet §4 declares no dependency on §3 or on that decision (its `data-links` is empty, and the ordering "Section 4 follows section 3" lives only in §8's prose).

findings.reason: the node must either be given the recorded payloads on a durable path or the clause restated to derive the figures from fixtures it builds, otherwise the assertion is unrunnable as written.
findings.text: §3's done-when requires "the three measured briefs above are asserted to fit their lanes after the change, using their recorded figures rather than re-derived ones", but §1's table at :47-75 is the only record of those briefs, their refusal payloads (161,013 / 508,965 / `graph_ops.py` 326,217) and the lane windows, and it names no path a test could open — while the repository requires a test to synthesise its inputs rather than reach outside the tree, so "recorded figures rather than re-derived ones" cannot both be honoured and executed.
